item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Integrated Approaches for Genetic Improvement, Selectio, and Development of Plant Materials Resistant to Xylella fastidiosa (CNR - Istituto di Bioscienze e Biorisorse)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-08 23:59
Institution: CNR - Istituto di Bioscienze e Biorisorse, Roma
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-14 Genetica

Through multidisciplinary approaches, the project aims to advance our understanding of the bacterium Xylella fastidiosa subsp. pauca and its infection mechanisms, as well as plant defence responses and the molecular basis of plant–pathogen interactions. The investigation of species of interest from the Mediterranean basin, alongside model species, will provide a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms and pathways involved in the response to infection. The development of innovative screening approaches will enable the rapid identification of resistant cultivars, significantly reducing the time required for screening due to the long growth cycle of olive trees. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-10 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-03 Zoologia e antropologia

The research activities will involve extracting DNA from archaeological sediments dating from the final Middle Palaeolithic to the Initial Upper Palaeolithic and collected during excavations conducted within the ERC Last Neanderthals project. Sedimentary DNA will be analysed using methodologies and protocols specifically designed for archaeological samples. The data generated through the laboratory work will subsequently be processed, analysed, and validated. The results will be interpreted within the archaeological and palaeoanthropological framework of the project. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Preclinical evaluation of the biodistribution, biological activity and therapeutic efficacy of recombinant TAT?-CDKL5 protein in models of CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The project will evaluate the biodistribution, biological activity and therapeutic efficacy of recombinant TAT?-CDKL5 protein in cellular and mouse models of CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder. Cellular studies will assess protein uptake, localization and persistence, together with effects on neuronal survival and maturation. Mouse studies will examine brain distribution, neuronal localization and pharmacodynamic responses to identify a dosing regimen for efficacy testing. Treatment effects will be assessed through behavioural testing and biochemical, histological and morphometric analyses, with particular attention to dendritic and synaptic alterations. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Mitochondrial bioenergetic remodelling in cellular dysfunction: the role of F1Fo-ATPase and respiratory supercomplexes as targets for novel mitoprotective strategies (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-07 Biochimica

The research will identify and characterise synthetic and natural molecules capable of counteracting mitochondrial dysfunction by modulating F1FO-ATPase and preserving respiratory supercomplex organisation. Biochemical, kinetic and bioenergetic analyses in isolated mitochondria and cellular models will assess the effects of selected compounds on ATP synthesis and hydrolysis, mitochondrial respiration, membrane potential, ROS production and calcium homeostasis. Respiratory supercomplex assembly and susceptibility to mitochondrial permeability transition will also be investigated. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-11 Farmacologia

Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive central nervous system malignancy in adults. This research project aims to identify novel druggable molecular targets to advance differentiation therapy strategies for glioblastoma (GBM). By inducing terminal differentiation of glioma stem cells (GSCs) and converting stem-like cells into non-stem states sensitive to conventional treatments, this project aims to reduce tumor intrinsic dynamic plasticity and achieve effective GBM eradication. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Analysis of cellular communication networks using single-cell multi-omics cancer data to identify novel anticancer therapies (Sc. Norm. Sup. PISA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-04 16:00
Institution: Sc. Norm. Sup. PISA, Pisa
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-08 Biologia molecolare

The successful candidate will analyze single-cell multi-omics data, such as transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic data, with a particular focus on interaction networks involved in cell–cell communication. Specifically, the candidate will be expected to develop innovative analytical algorithms for investigating cell–cell interaction motifs, with the aim of better elucidating the complex network of interactions between tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, as well as identifying novel therapeutic approaches.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Investigating systemic diurnal metabolic chasnges in heart failure (ref. D.R. 127/2026) (HUMANITAS University)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-06 12:00
Institution: HUMANITAS University, Pieve Emanuele - Milano
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-07 Biochimica

This project aims to elucidate how heart failure alters systemic and tissue-specific diurnal metabolism. Using TAC/sham mouse models, early, intermediate and advanced disease stages will be analysed by metabolic cages, glucose, pyruvate and insulin tolerance tests, plasma biochemistry and in vivo 13C-glucose tracing.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-03 13:00
Institution: Politecnica MARCHE, Ancona
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-10 Biologia cellulare e applicata

The research activity will focus on the development and application of innovative methodologies to investigate the occurrence, bioaccumulation, and ecotoxicological effects of emerging contaminants in marine ecosystems. Interactions between chemical contaminants and other stressors will also be assessed through integrated, effect-based approaches, contributing to the characterisation of the risks associated with exposure to complex mixtures of pollutants.
